plan-button-row.title: Button row (Mac order): dialog buttons, save and cancel, form actions
plan-button-row.note: Mac order, required in every dialog, sheet, form and confirmation (RuleUiActionRowMacOrder): right-aligned, the positive action rightmost and the default (Return), Cancel or Close immediately left of it (Esc), a destructive or third action alone at far left. Use it for dialog buttons, save cancel rows, form actions and confirm buttons: primary, cancel and destructive slots, equal shares on a phone. Only lays out buttons; for one button look take button. For the remove control take remove-control.

level-date-input.title: Date picker for a level
level-date-input.note: The date field of a level's popover in the value graph; the year rules are in date-rules. The Levels line's own dates are in value-levels-line. Plan.Value

remove-control.title: Remove control (delete button, red minus)
remove-control.note: Deletes the row it sits in; it calls the host and writes nothing itself. For a plain button take button.

card-group.title: Card group (framed group of a card)
card-group.note: Needs the card-mode provider; for a plain card surface take card. The person card's linked-person rows are not in it.

plan-card-facts.title: Plan card facts (sources, meters, status lines)
plan-card-facts.note: Facts on the record itself; Value child records are value-card-model, links plan-links-model. Not the older spec-card-facts.

value-card-model.title: Value card model
value-card-model.note: Pure read and fact builders for the Value and Development Resource card; writes are value-card-write, the screen is value-card. Plan.Value, Plan.DevelopmentResource

value-graph-geometry.title: Value graph geometry (axes, date ticks, bands)
value-graph-geometry.note: Math only; the drawn graph is value-graph.

type-picture.title: Type picture
type-picture.note: Draws a type's picture or nothing; as a button that opens the definition take type-term-popover.

plan-kinds.title: Plan card types and their lines
plan-kinds.note: Which lines each Plan type shows, in order; the drawn card is plan-card. Plan.Type

plan-links-model.title: Plan card links model (Part of, Solution of)
plan-links-model.note: Pure link reading and loop checks; the link lines on screen are plan-tag-links.

plan-impacts-model.title: Impacts model (Solution on Value and Resource)
plan-impacts-model.note: Pure; the Impacts table on screen is plan-impacts.

qualifier-value-picker.title: Qualifier value picker
qualifier-value-picker.note: Picks the value(s) of one Scale qualifier; to edit the qualifiers themselves take value-qualifiers-line. Plan.Value

sortable-tree.title: Sortable tree (drag and keyboard reorder)
sortable-tree.note: Reports drops and writes nothing; needs @dnd-kit/core 6.3.1. The Description editor that uses it is description-parts-view.

plan-stakeholders-model.title: Stakeholders, Authority and Resource Owner model
plan-stakeholders-model.note: Pure reading and constraint person rules; the lines on screen are plan-stakeholder-lines. Plan.DevelopmentResource

description-parts-model.title: Description parts model (Keyword parts)
description-parts-model.note: Parsing, tree, ordering and removal plans; the editor on screen is description-parts-view.

record-picker.title: Record picker (search and pick)
record-picker.note: The caller decides what is searched; for a GilbVeda type take type-chooser, for a Plan record by tag take plan-tag-picker.

entity-ref-value.title: Record reference shown by name
entity-ref-value.note: Shows a stored link as the record's name; includes GilbApp's refDisplayName (not entity-ref's).

field-row.title: Field row (click-to-edit text)
field-row.note: Text only, on a card with card-mode; for a controlled form field take field-control.

type-term-popover.title: Type definition popover
type-term-popover.note: Opens a type's definition and ontology link; to choose a type take type-chooser, for the picture alone take type-picture.

type-chooser.title: Type chooser (GilbVeda type search)
type-chooser.note: Search and pick a GilbVeda type; the Plan card's Type line is plan-type-field. For records take record-picker.

plan-type-field.title: Type field of a Plan card
plan-type-field.note: One GilbVeda type as a chip with the Replace question; the first line Type · Level · Version is plan-type-level-version. Plan.Type

plan-type-level-version.title: Type · Level · Version line
plan-type-level-version.note: The first line of every Plan card with the level chooser; the project's levels come from project-levels.

project-levels.title: Project levels (Business, Product, Solution)
project-levels.note: Reads and adds a project's levels for the level chooser; the line that shows them is plan-type-level-version.

plan-source.title: Source control (who said it)
plan-source.note: statedBy, derivedFrom or words for one Plan line; writes only through onCommit.

plan-tag-picker.title: Plan record picker by tag
plan-tag-picker.note: Links to a Plan record by its tag or creates one; the link lines themselves are plan-tag-links.

plan-stakeholder-lines.title: Stakeholder, Authority and Resource Owner lines
plan-stakeholder-lines.note: Three Plan card lines in one unit; the pure rules are plan-stakeholders-model. Plan.DevelopmentResource

plan-tag-links.title: Link lines (Part of, Sub-functions, Solution of)
plan-tag-links.note: Seven link lines of a Plan card; the picker alone is plan-tag-picker, the pure model plan-links-model.

plan-impacts.title: Impacts table of a Solution
plan-impacts.note: Impacts on Values and Development Resources; the pure model is plan-impacts-model.

help-doc.title: Help page building blocks
help-doc.note: Layout, sections, steps and notes of an in-app help page; the Description help is description-help.

description-help.title: Description help panel
description-help.note: Help for writing a Description in Keyword parts; built from help-doc.

description-parts-view.title: Description editor (Keyword parts)
description-parts-view.note: Draws and edits the Description as a tree of parts; the pure model is description-parts-model, the drag tree sortable-tree.

value-graph.title: Value graph (Scale arrow and timeline)
value-graph.note: Draws and drags levels and never writes; the card line that holds it is value-illustration, the math value-graph-geometry. Plan.Value

value-card-write.title: Value card write layer
value-card-write.note: Saves levels, qualifiers, meters and Scale as child records; a read-only Value card does not need it. Plan.Value

value-scale-line.title: Scale line of a Value card
value-scale-line.note: Unit, rate, context and direction; writes through onChange. The qualifiers of the Scale are value-qualifiers-line. Plan.Value

value-qualifiers-line.title: Qualifiers line of a Value card
value-qualifiers-line.note: Edits the Scale qualifiers and their options; to pick a qualifier's value take qualifier-value-picker. Plan.Value

value-endpoint-line.title: Endpoint line of a Value card
value-endpoint-line.note: Subject and Reference types with pictures; writes through onChange. Plan.Value

value-meters-line.title: Meters line of a Value card
value-meters-line.note: Each Meter with its Human, AI and Instrument lines; writes through onChange. Plan.Value

value-levels-line.title: Levels line of a Value card (Goal, Budget)
value-levels-line.note: Every level with number, date, qualifiers and source; the drawn graph is value-graph. Plan.Value, Plan.DevelopmentResource

value-illustration.title: Illustration line of a Value card
value-illustration.note: The card line around value-graph; for the graph alone take value-graph. Plan.Value

plan-card.title: Plan card engine
plan-card.note: One engine for all four Plan cards; to start from one card take function-card, solution-card, value-card or resource-card.

function-card.title: Function card
function-card.note: The whole card for a Function or Function Constraint; for one line take its line unit. Built on plan-card.

solution-card.title: Solution card
solution-card.note: The whole card for a Solution or Solution Constraint; for one line take its line unit. Built on plan-card.

value-card.title: Value card
value-card.note: The whole Value card; for one line take its line unit (value-scale-line, value-levels-line …). Built on plan-card. Plan.Value

resource-card.title: Development Resource card
resource-card.note: The whole Development Resource card (Budget, Resource Owner); it is the Value card for t:Resource. Built on plan-card. Plan.DevelopmentResource

plan-card-hosts-gilbplatform.title: Plan card host for GilbPlatform (one provider for all four Plan cards)
plan-card-hosts-gilbplatform.note: Take this to draw the Function, Solution, Value and Development Resource cards on GilbPlatform with no host object written: one provider sets the origins and the session. It is not a card; the cards are function-card, solution-card, value-card and resource-card, built on plan-card. For one host alone use its factories. Plan.Value, Plan.DevelopmentResource

own-card.title: Own card finder (my profile card in a vault)
own-card.note: Finds the signed-in person's own card (my profile card, self card) in a vault by hard identity: the derived id or the vault's profile pointer, never by name or email. It reads through a transport you inject. To only compute the card's id and address with no read take self-card; to use the finding as the source of what a person writes take plan-self-source.

plan-self-source.title: Own card as the source of what a person writes (useSelfSource)
plan-self-source.note: The signed-in person's own card as the a:statedBy source of a Plan line: finds it once in the landing vault and answers its address or nothing. Never by email or display name. The finding itself is own-card; the id alone is self-card. Plan.Value, Plan.DevelopmentResource

stakeholder-kinds.title: Stakeholder kinds and their words (read from the master)
stakeholder-kinds.note: Which kinds of record may be a stakeholder (Person, Organization and the like) and their labels, read from the GilbVeda master, kept across sessions and shared per page; "not known yet" is never "none". For the lines on a Plan card take plan-stakeholder-lines; for its rules take plan-stakeholders-model. Plan.DevelopmentResource

lws-records.title: Record client (read, create, change, retype one record)
lws-records.note: The typed client for one record in a vault over the platform's record interface (record client): read, create, patch and retype, with the typed errors a refused write throws. For a list of records take lws-vault-sets or record-sync; for a screen's list with create, retype and delete take plan-record-hooks; for the credential it signs with see lws-session-bridge.

lws-vault-sets.title: Vault sets (what a vault holds: pages, find, text search)
lws-vault-sets.note: Asks a vault what it holds: a page of its records or files, a find by attribute, a text search, with a cap on requests in flight. It reads and writes no single record; for one record take lws-records. For only what changed since a stored position take record-sync.

record-sync.title: Record sync (record list and change feed)
record-sync.note: A vault's typed record list and only what changed in it since a stored position, through the authenticated fetch the host injects. No React and no credential of its own. For one record take lws-records; for a text search or attribute find take lws-vault-sets; for the screen hooks take plan-record-hooks.

plan-record-hooks.title: Record list hooks (scrolling list; create, retype, delete)
plan-record-hooks.note: React hooks for a scrolling list of a vault's records and the three changes a person makes (create, retype, delete): each shown at once, written in the background, the cache put back on error. Needs a query client. For a single read or write without React take lws-records; the cache it uses is record-cache-kit.

lws-relations.title: Relation client (write, read, end a relation)
lws-relations.note: Links between two records only; for one record take lws-records, for a page or find take lws-vault-sets. Not a sign-in and not a cache of relations.

platform-fetch.title: Signed platform fetch
platform-fetch.note: Only the fetch that signs each call; the sign-in is signin, the credential seam is lws-session-bridge. It holds no credential and does not retry.

main-tag.title: Main tag of a record (read, cached)
main-tag.note: Only reads a main tag, never writes one; the name shown for a record is entity-ref-value or record-cache-kit. For the tag calls themselves take tag-client.

ontology-reads.title: Ontology term reads (definition, picture, search)
ontology-reads.note: Public reads with no credential and no writes; it has no built-in ontology host. For a vault record take lws-records.

online-stakeholder-card.title: Online stakeholder card (person with no record)
online-stakeholder-card.note: Read-only card of a person from the holder's circles who has no record, with an offer to make the holder's own card; for a card that merges both take one-card, for the Plan cards take plan-card.

stakeholder-card-hosts-gilbplatform.title: Stakeholder card host for GilbPlatform
stakeholder-card-hosts-gilbplatform.note: The ready-made GilbPlatform host for the Stakeholder entry card, so it draws, reads and adds with no host object written; for the Plan cards take plan-card-hosts-gilbplatform.

reachable-vaults.title: Vaults the signed-in person can reach
reachable-vaults.note: Reads the reachable vaults with names, parents and landing flag, and decorates the session's vault set; it does not search or page records, for that take lws-vault-sets.

contact-rows.title: Contact rows (Email, Phone, Social, Skills)
contact-rows.note: Edits any number of Email, Phone, Social and Skills rows of a person; it is not the stakeholder's Relations or Contact-preferences fields, which are stakeholder-set-fields.

stakeholder-set-fields.title: Stakeholder Relations and Contact-preferences fields
stakeholder-set-fields.note: Draws and edits only the Relations and Contact-preferences fields from the ontology's field set; for Email, Phone and Social rows take contact-rows.

org-employees.title: Organization employees (inline and searchable sheet)
org-employees.note: Lists an organization's employees inline and in a searchable sheet; for its parent and units take org-hierarchy, for its logo take org-mark.

org-hierarchy.title: Organization parent and units
org-hierarchy.note: Shows and edits an organization's parent organization and units; for its employees take org-employees, for its logo take org-mark.

org-mark.title: Organization logo
org-mark.note: Draws an organization's logo from a bounded file fetch; for a person's or vault's photo take vault-profile-photo or grantee-face.

stakeholder-find.title: Find existing people by name as you type
stakeholder-find.note: Looks up the holder's existing records of a name while typing, before a new one is made; it creates nothing, for that take person-create.

kind-relation.title: Tie a person to a kind of contact
kind-relation.note: Writes and ends the tie between a person and a kind of contact, with race guards; for any other link between records take lws-relations.

person-create.title: Create a person record
person-create.note: Makes a person record in a named vault, finding candidate people first; for a general record write take lws-records, and for a lookup alone take stakeholder-find.

vault-profile-photo.title: Vault profile photo
vault-profile-photo.note: Finds and loads a vault's own profile photo and makes the vault's own card when it has none; for a photo another person shares with the viewer take grantee-face.

grantee-face.title: Photo another person shares with you
grantee-face.note: Loads the profile photo another person shares with the viewer; for a vault's own photo take vault-profile-photo.

one-card.title: Merged stakeholder card (theirs and yours)
one-card.note: Draws one merged card per person, the holder's rows and the person's rows in one frame; for a person with no record take online-stakeholder-card.

stakeholder-list-reader.title: Stakeholders list reader
stakeholder-list-reader.note: Reads a holder's stakeholders, records and online people into one deduplicated list with names and photos, within a request budget; it draws nothing.

birthday-picker.title: Birthday picker
birthday-picker.note: Picks a birthday from day, month and an optional year with no free text; for a date at a level take level-date-input.

online-card.title: Link a record to the person's online card
online-card.note: Finds, links, unlinks and refreshes the link between a holder's record of a person and that person's own online card; for the card itself take online-stakeholder-card.

stakeholder-record-card.title: Stakeholder record card (a holder's own record of a person)
stakeholder-record-card.note: The whole card of a person the holder keeps a record of, with Edit, +, the groups in their order, autosave, addresses, languages, skills, interests, employment and the link to their online card; for a person with no record take online-stakeholder-card, and to mount it on GilbPlatform take stakeholder-record-card-host-gilbplatform.

stakeholder-record-card-host-gilbplatfor.title: Stakeholder record card host for GilbPlatform
stakeholder-record-card-host-gilbplatfor.note: The ready-made GilbPlatform host for the Stakeholder record card, so it draws, reads and saves with no host object written; mount it inside the provider of stakeholder-card-hosts-gilbplatform. For the online card's host take stakeholder-card-hosts-gilbplatform.

language-section.title: Languages group of a person card (name and flag)
language-section.note: The Languages group of a held person card: the languages by name and flag, add, flag, remove, mark the contact language, make private; it is part of stakeholder-record-card, so take that for the whole card.

skill-rows.title: Skills section with a held note under each skill
skill-rows.note: A person card's Skills section with the held note, who added it and the private or shared switch under each picked skill; for the plain Skills rows with no notes take contact-rows.

skill-picker-sheet.title: Skill picker sheet (search the catalogue, set a depth)
skill-picker-sheet.note: A bottom sheet that searches the live skill catalogue and lets the holder pick a skill with its depth; for the Skills section that draws it take skill-rows.

interest-rows.title: Interests section with a held note under each interest
interest-rows.note: A person card's Interests: each with its note, who added it and who sees it, add from the catalogue and remove; for Skills take skill-rows.

held-notes.title: Held notes (what a holder keeps about someone, private or shared)
held-notes.note: Reads and writes the notes a person keeps about someone in their own vault, private or shared with that person, one claim per note; for the rows that draw them take skill-rows or interest-rows.

employment-rows.title: Employment section of a person record
employment-rows.note: The whole Employment section of a person card over the record's employment edges, in the card's modes (read, edit, add, remove); for the state alone take employments-state, for one framed group take employment-card.

employment-card.title: Employment card (a person's employments as a framed group)
employment-card.note: One person's employments as a framed group: company, role dates, titles; add, edit and remove, over an editor you hand in; for the section already wired to a record take employment-rows.

employments-state.title: Employments state (load, add, edit, remove, each write queued)
employments-state.note: A React hook that reads a person record's employments, adds, edits and removes them one write at a time, with no drawing; for the section that draws them take employment-rows.

company-search.title: Company box (type a name, pick an organization record)
company-search.note: The company box of an employment: type a name, pick a matching organization record or use the name as typed, and it says which vault it searched; for the whole Employment section take employment-rows.

speed-kit.title: Speed kit (open from a copy, update behind)
speed-kit.note: The five speed units behind one entry, wired to one app name with a clean sign-out; take it for a whole app. For one part take the unit itself: device-store, session-cache, prefetch-registry, background-jobs or principal-hub.

device-store.title: Device store (copy of what an app read)
device-store.note: The copy kept in the browser per person and workspace, as a starting point and never an answer, bounded to 25 MB. For the copy in memory only take session-cache; for the hook that shows it take use-cached.

session-cache.title: Memory copy of what a page read
session-cache.note: An in-memory copy keyed by person and workspace that a page opens from at once and revalidates behind, bounded by entries and bytes. For the copy that survives a reload take device-store; for the React hook take use-cached.

use-cached.title: Page data from the copy (React hook)
use-cached.note: Only the hook that renders from the session cache and says when an update runs; it needs session-cache for the cache itself. For the "Updated 14:05" line take updated-line.

prefetch-registry.title: Page warmers (load before the person asks)
prefetch-registry.note: Only the registry that starts a page's loads on hover or idle, once per workspace in the stale window, skipping heavy ones on a slow link. It does not hold the copy: that is session-cache.

principal-hub.title: Whose session this tab is (clears caches on change)
principal-hub.note: Only the one place that knows whose tab it is and clears every registered cache when the person changes; it holds no credential. For signing in take signin; for the copy itself take session-cache.

background-jobs.title: Background jobs (outlive the page)
background-jobs.note: Only the store of jobs that outlive the page: one flight per key, one lane per workspace, never retried, failures kept as notices. For the cached read take session-cache; for the clear on sign-out take principal-hub.

updated-line.title: Updated line (Updating... / Updated 14:05)
updated-line.note: Only the status line, the stale note and the refresh-button feedback; the data and the hook are use-cached. For a plain button take button.

speed-meter.title: Speed readings (requests, page paint, writes)
speed-meter.note: An in-memory meter an app calls so it reports speed readings: requests received and answered by route, the time from a page's start to its first rows and to the full list with where the rows came from, the start of the read copy, and write timings. It only records; Speed Lab judges. For the copy itself take speed-kit; for the line that says when data was updated take updated-line.

place-claims-card.title: Address group of a card (a person's addresses, add form)
place-claims-card.note: The whole Address group of a person card: each stored address, a plain-text address the record already holds, and the add form that saves as a place is picked; it writes nothing itself. For the section already wired to the vault take address-rows, and for the data and the save acts alone take use-place-claims.

address-rows.title: Address section of a person record
address-rows.note: The whole Address section of a person record: reads the person's addresses from the vault that holds the record, draws them as a card group and saves, changes and removes them there; for a card you wire yourself take place-claims-card with use-place-claims. Place names are read from the place catalogue only (GET, credentials omitted); nothing is written there.

place-picker.title: Place box (search the catalogue, pick a city, region or country)
place-picker.note: The box where a place is searched in the shared place catalogue and chosen at one rung, each hit with what it is and where; a failed search says so and never says the place does not exist. Catalogue reads are GET only, to the catalogue's origin, credentials omitted; for a role's work place take work-location-field.

place-claims.title: Addresses of a person (read from the vault)
place-claims.note: Only the read of a person's addresses from the vault that holds them: the address claims and their field claims, and whether the whole vault was read. For the writing take place-claim-write; for the read with the save, change and remove acts together take use-place-claims.

use-place-claims.title: Addresses of a record, with save, change, remove (React hook)
use-place-claims.note: The hook that reads a record's addresses, tells apart not known, reading, failed, incomplete and ready, and saves, changes and removes one with a read-back; it needs place-claims and place-claim-write. For only the read take place-claims, and for the drawn section take address-rows.

place-claim-write.title: Addresses of a person (write to the vault)
place-claim-write.note: Only the writing of a person's addresses to the vault that holds them: create, change and remove, one request per fact, and a write aimed at the place catalogue is refused before any request. For the read take place-claims; for the state and the acts together take use-place-claims.

geo-catalogue.title: Place catalogue reads (search, one place, walk up to the country)
geo-catalogue.note: The client of the shared place catalogue with no screen: search by kind of place, one place, the walk up to its country. Reads go only to the origin set with geo-origin, GET only, credentials omitted, and an address outside the catalogue is refused before any request; for a drawn box take place-picker.

work-location-field.title: Work place box of a role (search and pick by name)
work-location-field.note: The box where a role's work place is searched in the place catalogue and chosen, showing the place by name and saying when the name could not be read; it stores nothing itself. Catalogue reads are GET only, credentials omitted; for the read-only name take work-place-name, and for a person's addresses take address-rows.

work-place-name.title: Work place of a role, drawn by name (read only)
work-place-name.note: Draws a role's work place by its name with what it is and where, or says plainly when the name is not known; it is the place-name slot of employment-card. For choosing the place take work-location-field.

site-footer.title: Site Footer (website)
site-footer.note: Not a sitemap or mega footer, a newsletter block (take newsletter-signup) or a language strip (take language-switcher): one short list of links and a copyright line.

site-logo.title: Site Logo (website)
site-logo.note: Not a brand lockup system, a light/dark logo switch or the site's config or router: one home link with image, wordmark or both.

titled-section.title: Titled Section (website)
titled-section.note: Not a hero (take hero) and not the pill-and-headline band (take section-heading); no picture beside the title, no background, no motion.

mega-menu.title: Mega Menu (website)
mega-menu.note: Not the header or its open button (take hide-on-scroll-header or your own) and not a dropdown per item; it is one sheet that the header opens.

waitlist-form.title: Waitlist Signup Form (website)
waitlist-form.note: Not a newsletter signup (take newsletter-signup) or a contact form (take contact-form), and it stores nothing; the server must run validate again.

grain-overlay.title: Grain Overlay (website)
grain-overlay.note: Not an animated noise, a filter on a scrolling container or a background for one section; it is one fixed film-grain over the whole page.

parallax-layer.title: Parallax Layer (website)
parallax-layer.note: Not a scroll-linked fade or reveal (take scroll-frame) or a pinned section (take sticky-card-deck); not for content a reader must read.

double-bezel.title: Double Bezel (website)
double-bezel.note: Not a device frame (take device-frame), a text card or anything that moves; it only mounts a picture in a two-layer frame.

shimmer-headline.title: Shimmer Headline (website)
shimmer-headline.note: Not a text colour, a loop, or a fade or rise (take scroll-frame); one highlight sweep when the heading first scrolls into view.

picture-upload.title: Picture upload
picture-upload.note: Uploads bytes only; to make the sizes take picture-shrink, to upload and link all sizes with resume take picture-set.

picture-viewer.title: Picture viewer (full screen, photo-app gestures)
picture-viewer.note: Only shows pictures from URLs you give it; it does not shrink, sign or upload. For a signed thumbnail from a vault take signed-picture.

picture-shrink.title: Picture shrink / resize (thumbnail, WebP)
picture-shrink.note: Makes smaller bytes only and sends nothing; to send them take picture-upload. It is not a cropper. The full-size copy is optional (sizes.full: false).

signed-picture.title: Signed picture / thumbnail from a vault
signed-picture.note: Shows a picture that needs a signed request; a public picture is a plain img. To upload take picture-upload, to shrink picture-shrink. Also found as: picture bytes; download the original picture; read a picture's bytes.

picture-pick.title: Add picture (camera, choose, paste, drop)
picture-pick.note: Hands back the chosen files only and does not check the bytes; to shrink them take picture-shrink, to send them picture-upload. Also found as: take a photo with the camera; camera photo; choose a picture; paste or drop a picture.

signin.title: Sign-in and start-up (sign in, open the app's own vault, create a named vault, list vaults)
signin.note: Sign in and start-up: useLiveStart({ credential, idOrigin, app, vaultConfig }) restores the sign-in or shows the card, opens the person's own app vault (a first sign-in creates it, once) and answers { stage: signin | opening | ready | error, vault, error, retry, signOut } - the whole live-app start-up in about 15 lines; createLiveStart is the same without React. Also the sign-in card, the DPoP proof, the session credential and a machine agent's sign-in, with creating a named vault and listing a person's vaults (each with its short name). makeSignInAuth builds the card's auth in one call. ensureAppVault / createAppVaultService find or make the person's own app vault once (a 202 is finished, not duplicated). For the signed fetch alone take platform-fetch; for the vault list with parents take reachable-vaults; a passkey is host wiring, not this unit. Also found as: sign in; sign-in; start-up; start up; open app vault; first sign-in creates the person's own app vault; create vault on first sign-in; sign in and make a vault.

vault-access.title: Vault access (grant, revoke, share a whole vault)
vault-access.note: Who may use a whole vault: grant, revoke, read the access list, share to view or edit. For a share of one record take lws-relations; for which vaults you can reach take reachable-vaults. Exports the Control refusal sentence (NO_CONTROL). Share access grant: give a person's vault read or write on yours.

fake-platform.title: Fake platform (test stand-in: sign-in, records, files, grants)
fake-platform.note: For tests only, never in an app's shipped code: it keeps state in memory and checks no signatures. To call the platform take lws-records, signin, picture-set or vault-access. Refuses a parentVault the caller did not mint, as the platform does.

picture-set.title: Picture sizes upload and copy map (a picture's copies in a vault: list, thumbnail, largest, store, end)
picture-set.note: Picture copies in a vault: remembers what was uploaded and linked, with resume and a retry of the small copy's link (storePictureSet), loads the vault's copy map once (loadCopyMap, copiesOf, thumbUriOf, largestUriOf), lists a vault's files and ends a file or a picture's copies (copiesToEnd); the upload itself is picture-upload, the shrinking picture-shrink, the retry save-queue. It does not link a picture to a record.

picture-errors.title: Picture error messages
picture-errors.note: Turns a thrown value into words; it does not catch, log or retry (retry is save-queue). For the access-denied screen take refusal-detail.

save-queue.title: Offline save queue (per person, retry)
save-queue.note: Holds the queue and its rules on this device only; it sends nothing and has no loop, so the host sends and retries. Not a way to move work between devices.

refusal-detail.title: Access denied screen and refusal line
refusal-detail.note: For a refused read; it classifies nothing and sends nothing. The banner for a refused write is the app's own words. Entry ./describe turns any error into one plain sentence to show (error message): no access, vault busy, a platform refusal sentence, sign in again, changed elsewhere, no connection. Also found as: error message; describe an error; error sentence; friendly error text.

text-filter.title: Text filter / search (accent-insensitive)
text-filter.note: Answers true or false for a word found anywhere in the text; it does not rank or highlight. For word-prefix search take search-tokens.

style-runtime.title: Apply the app's style at start (style tokens)
style-runtime.note: loadStyle writes the CSS custom properties from one style.tokens.json, validated, no flash, with an offline fallback. Every new app takes it by default.

style-studio.title: App Style Studio (choose the app's style before building)
style-studio.note: Choose the app's colours (palettes incl. after Sanzo Wada, one seed colour, or read from your website), fonts, buttons, windows and logo before building, and save them to the app's resource vault or the dev server. From website works with the app's session through makeExtractFromUrl({ baseUrl, credential }); makeDevServerSave and splitLogo save to a dev server. A developer tool, taken once.

style-app-files.title: App style files (dev save endpoint and font export, Node)
style-app-files.note: Node only: the Vite dev middleware that writes style.tokens.json and brand-logo.png from the Studio's save, and the command and function that copy the chosen @fontsource woff2 files into public/fonts and write fonts.css. For the screen that chooses the style take style-studio; to apply it in the page take style-runtime.

lws-session-bridge.title: Start-up for a live app (base origin, session credential, signed fetch)
lws-session-bridge.note: configureLiveApp sets the base origin, the system-vault hosts and the session credential in one call, and the credential then signs every platform call (signedSend, dpopReadAuth, dpopWriteAuth). For the signed fetch alone take platform-fetch; the sign-in card and the credential are in signin.

vault-list.title: Vault list helpers (label, tree order, writable, choices of own and shared)
vault-list.note: Pure functions over the list of vaults a person reaches: label, tree order, writable ones, the root of a named vault, and the chooser rows with own first and shared labelled (vaultChoices, choiceLine); also remembering the chosen vault and the shared-with-you offer in the app's own key-value store (rememberVault, rememberedVault, sharedOffer, dismissOffer). No React and no fetching; the list itself is reachable-vaults or signin's listVaults. Also found as: vault chooser; list of vaults shared with you; vaults of one type; remember the chosen vault; shared with you banner.

vault-address.title: Vault address check (is this string a vault address)
vault-address.note: Shape only: tells a vault address from a person, a WebID or a record. It is not a lookup and does not find a vault by email or name.

photo-ref.title: Photo reference (which file a stored picture names, and the address of its bytes)
photo-ref.note: Reads a stored photo reference: the file it names and the absolute address its bytes live at, on the door the record was read through. Pure; it fetches nothing. To show the picture take signed-picture.

vault-picture-viewer.title: Vault picture viewer (open a stored picture full screen, signed)
vault-picture-viewer.note: Opens a vault picture in the full-screen viewer: thumbnail first, then the largest copy, both fetched signed; also a local picture with no fetch. Loads the viewer's CSS itself. Needs picture-viewer, signed-picture and picture-set.

record-picture.title: Record picture link and flow (attach, replace, remove or delete a record's picture, with the files ended in the right order)
record-picture.note: Attaches a stored picture to a record's picture fact (a PATCH with If-Match, read back to check the link stuck, both the string and the link forms read), and runs the add, replace, remove and delete order so no picture file is orphaned: record-first or picture-first, old files ended only after the new link held, files ended before the record is deleted. Also checks a picked file (type, 25 MB) and shrinks it to a screen copy and a thumbnail with EXIF and GPS dropped, and binds picture-set to one vault. The fact name is always passed in; it holds no term. The upload itself is picture-set, the shrinking picture-shrink, the record calls lws-records. Also found as: record picture; attach a photo to a record; take or upload a record's picture; picture service per vault; release picture URLs; flow deps for a vault; stamp who stated a record.

modal-sheet.title: Modal sheet (dialog: Escape, backdrop, focus kept, scroll locked)
modal-sheet.note: One shared dialog: a titled panel, bottom sheet on a phone and a card above 600px, closes on Escape or a backdrop click, traps Tab, returns focus, locks page scroll; imports its own CSS. Draws in place, no portal. For the share dialog take vault-share-sheet. For a full-screen picture take picture-viewer.

vault-share-sheet.title: Vault share sheet (give, see and remove access to a whole vault)
vault-share-sheet.note: Share your vault with a person by their vault name or address: who has access, edit or view, inline remove. Headless ./model plus a React sheet on modal-sheet. The calls themselves are vault-access; a share of one record is lws-relations. Share access grant: the sheet for it. Also found as: share; give access; invite; who has access; owner. Takes a help line under the title, shows your own row as You, and remembers the name you typed for each person.

optimistic-records.title: Optimistic record list (add, edit, delete and undo shown at once, a failed write rolled back)
optimistic-records.note: One React hook, useRecordList({ list, create, update, remove, key, undoMs, sort, onProblem }): add, edit and delete are shown at once; a failed write is rolled back and reported; a delete waits undoMs (default 10 s) for undo(id) before remove is called, several can wait together; flushPending() makes them real now (sign-out, vault switch) and unmount or a hidden page does the same. Writes to one record go one after another. No data library; the four calls are yours. Also found as: record list; add, edit, delete; undo delete; optimistic; offline-friendly list; undo bar.

vault-switcher.title: Vault switcher (a chip with the open vault and a sheet to pick another)
vault-switcher.note: A chip with the open vault's name; a tap opens a sheet listing the vaults the person reaches, own first, shared and view-only ones labelled, the open one marked, and calls onPick with the chosen vault. React, on modal-sheet and vault-list (vaultChoices, choiceLine). It lists with the load you pass; the list itself is reachable-vaults or signin's listVaults. Also found as: vault chooser; choose a vault; pick another vault; switch between shared vaults; switch vault; several vaults; shared with me; vault picker. The hook useVaultChoice({ listed, ownVaultId, principal, appKey, represents?, store? }) holds the choice for you: options (own first), current, switchTo, markGone and canWrite, remembered per person and app, a gone vault dropped.

zip.title: Zip file (write stored files, read them back)
zip.note: Pure bytes in, bytes out, no DOM and no React: zipStore packs named files into a zip with no compression, UTF-8 names and a fixed date so the same input gives the same bytes; unzipStore reads the files back and checks each checksum; crc32. It refuses unsafe names (empty, leading /, .. parts, repeats) and anything over 4 GiB. A zip with deflate inside is refused by name of the method; for compressed zips take a library. Also found as: zip file; make a zip; pack files into an archive; unzip; read a zip; export as zip.

csp-headers.title: CSP headers (one policy file to meta tag, dev header and _headers)
csp-headers.note: Vite plugin, Node only: reads one policy file (default security/csp.txt) and writes the Content-Security-Policy meta tag into index.html (without frame-ancestors, which a meta tag cannot carry), sets the header on the dev and preview servers, and writes or merges dist/_headers for Cloudflare Pages. Per-app parts come in as exclude and transformPolicy; the pure helpers readPolicy, metaPolicy, headersFileText need no Vite. Needs no vite package. Also found as: content security policy; CSP header; security headers; _headers file; Cloudflare headers; meta CSP.

browser-proof.title: Browser proof (headless Chrome end-to-end harness)
browser-proof.note: Node test helper, no packages, no React: startBrowser launches headless Chrome with a throwaway profile in a folder you name and gives a page (goto, eval, waitFor, screenshot, consoleErrors, key, setViewport); runLegs runs named legs, prints PASS or FAIL for each, fails a leg that logged a page error, and exits non-zero on any FAIL. Chrome and its helpers are stopped and the profile removed, even on failure. Also found as: browser test; end-to-end test; headless Chrome; e2e harness; take screenshots in a test.

vault-export.title: Vault export (records and their pictures in one archive, read back)
vault-export.note: The generic export: list the records, map each to JSON with the app's own function, read each record's picture bytes, pack the records file and the pictures into one archive, read the archive back and compare, and answer { zipBytes, count, files, pictures, differences }. A picture that cannot be read is named in differences, never thrown. Listing, bytes and zip are passed in (lws-records or vault-records-of-type, signed-picture's pictureBytes, zip's zipStore and unzipStore), so it has no peers. Also found as: export records; export as zip; download my data; back up a vault.

since-last-visit.title: Since your last visit (what changed, new records, activity banner)
since-last-visit.note: Remembers what a list looked like at the person's last visit and says what other people added, changed or deleted since: new records, changes, activity, a dismissible banner. Headless readVisit / writeVisit / diffVisit / recordVisit on the listing the app already has (ids, updatedAt, statedBy); own changes are left out and the first visit shows nothing. Per device, on the device clock; a delete cannot say who. SinceBanner is the optional React banner, plain CSS over the style tokens. Also found as: since your last visit; what changed; new records; changes; activity; banner.

section-menu.title: Header menu (menu, more, three dots, section menu panel)
section-menu.note: The app's header menu: a three-dots "..." MenuButton (menu, more, overflow; Escape and outside click close it, focus returns to the button, arrow keys move) and the SectionMenu, a header button that opens a large panel of sections and options. Takes its sections and acts as data; the three-dots menu takes a short list of items. For placing a menu inside the visible band take menu-place. Also found as: menu; more; three dots; header menu; overflow menu; kebab menu; dropdown menu.
